Subject: Unexpected jump on Oct 20–25 usage — invoice 12345

Hi Rachel,

Hope you’re well. We just received invoice_12345 for Oct activity and noticed a ~3.2x increase in billed tokens for embedding requests between Oct 20–25 compared to our expected baseline. Our internal tracing shows no corresponding increase in API calls from our app during that period.

Key details:
- Invoice: invoice_12345
- Billed tokens (embeddings): 12,350,412
- Our expected based on logs: ~3,900,000 tokens
- VAT charged on full amount (we are VAT-registered in the UK; our VAT ID is GB999888777)

Could you please: 1) provide the token-level metering snapshot Redwoods has for our account for Oct 1–31, 2) confirm whether any automatic model fallback, replay, or retry behavior could have produced duplicate token billing, and 3) confirm VAT treatment — we expected VAT reversal on exported services.

We’re prepared to pay the reconciled amount promptly but need the variance explained before we process payment.

Thanks,
Amy Fox

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected jump on Oct 20–25 usage — invoice_12345 (analysis)

Summary of findings after correlating the billing engine logs and serving traces:

1) Root cause: model fallback + duplicated completions
- On Oct 20 at ~03:12 UTC we observed a region-wide autoscaling event that briefly routed a subset of ACME requests from an optimized embedding service (quantized model v2) to a compatibility fallback instance running the non-quantized embedding model. The fallback path does not share KV caching for prefixes, so some repeated prefix work was re-executed and billed.
- In addition, for a 15-minute window (03:10–03:25 UTC) our retry logic retried a small percentage (~1.8%) of requests due to an upstream networking blip — those retries were billed and not deduplicated in the post-process (bug ticket below).

2) Measured impact:
- Duplicate/extra tokens from fallback + retries during Oct 20 window: ~7,850,000 tokens
- Remaining variance vs your baseline likely explained by a higher-than-typical batch size in your job run on Oct 21 that increased per-request token generation slightly (~600k tokens).
- Total reconciliation: billed 12,350,412 vs adjusted expected 4,000,000 => net confirmed extra ~8,350,412 tokens (within rounding of logs).

3) VAT treatment:
- Our billing flow mistakenly applied VAT on the gross amount. Because ACME provided a valid UK VAT ID, VAT should have been zero-rated under exported services rules. We will reissue the invoice without VAT and apply the tax correction.

4) Remediation and next steps:
- We will issue a credit for the overbilled tokens equal to 8,350,412 tokens at your contracted unit rate (see attached adjustment invoice).
- We opened internal bug BILL-3421 to deduplicate billed retries in post-processing and to ensure fallback paths share prefix cache when possible.
- Proposed customer-facing materials: updated invoice (attached) + a one-page root-cause note.

Attachments: usage_report_202610.pdf (includes per-hour charts), invoice_202610_acme_12345_adjusted.pdf (adjusted, credit applied)

Let me know if you want the raw per-request IDs exported — those are a larger file but we can send an S3 link.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

Subject: Re: Unexpected jump on Oct 20–25 usage — invoice 12345 (resolution)

Hi Amy —

Thanks for your patience. Summary and actions:

- What happened: a short autoscaling/fallback event + a small replay spike on Oct 20 resulted in approximately 8.35M extra tokens billed. Our post-processing did not dedupe those retry billings.
- VAT: we will reissue without VAT; your UK VAT ID has been applied and the corrected invoice is attached.
- Compensation: we issued a credit for the overbilled token amount at your contracted rate; net amount due is now reduced on the attached adjusted invoice.
- Preventive fix: BILL-3421 is prioritized for the next sprint to dedupe retries and add an alert when fallback routing increases token cost by >20% in an hour.

Attached: usage_report_202610.pdf, invoice_202610_acme_12345_adjusted.pdf
Links: DocuSign for invoice acceptance (https://app.docusign.com/ACME/REDWOOD/INV-12345)

If that looks good I can have our billing team apply the credit and re-send a zero-VAT invoice so you can process the payment for the adjusted balance.

Best,
